newsitem.title: UK: Matthew Clark slides as worries continue.
newsitem.headline: Matthew Clark slides as worries continue.

text.p: Shares in troubled cider maker Matthew Clark tumbled again on Friday, unable to shake off worries that have surrounded the group since a profits warning a month ago, analysts said.
Matthew Clark stunned investors in September, when a warning that increased competition from new "alcopop" drinks had hit summer sales sent the stock sliding over 50 percent.
The shares fell another 10 percent today and at 286p are nearly 60 percent below their pre-warning September 9 price.
Traders said a round of visits to analysts by rival group H.P. Bulmer Holdings has served to underline the problem as specific to Matthew Clark rather than the industry.
Bulmer shares, up 2-1/2p to 520p today, had suffered from the fallout from Clark's warning, losing over 10 percent in the past month.
After meeting analysts over the past couple of days, Bulmer is due to meet with institutional shareholders today.
"The position is pretty grim for Clark. It needs to advertise more and that's going to cost them," said one analyst.

"Equally we don't think they've run into cashflow problems and so their dividend is not necessarily under threat and should provide a bit of support. However, it's hard to conceive of anyone being a buyer of the stock," the analsyt said.
